 TL is S.’s longest poem in terza rima, a form he had been experimenting with since 1817:
his first long composition in tercets is the incomplete Athanase (Longman ii, no. 146) and
he adapted the form in the fourteen-line stanzas of OWW. These earlier uses are generally
more punctuated and end-stopped than the freer and faster verse of TL. In the summer
of 1820 S. translated Dante’s Matilda episode into English terza rima (Dante’s Purgatorio
Canto XXVIII, 1–51) and, at Pisa in December 1820, used terza rima, and the same hen-
decasyllable line as the Commedia, to write the Dantescan fragment The Tower of Famine
